saint-gobain.name: Saint-Gobain
saint-gobain.summary: Saint-Gobain is a France-headquartered building-materials group whose main direct emissions come from energy-intensive glass melting, gypsum/plasterboard, insulation, mortars, pipe/cast products and related quarrying/mineral feedstock operations, with major emitting industrial footprints in France, the United States, India, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, Brazil and China.

orlen.name: ORLEN
orlen.summary: ORLEN is a Polish integrated energy and petrochemical group whose largest direct emissions come mainly from oil refineries and petrochemical/CHP assets in Poland, Lithuania and Czechia, with additional upstream oil and gas operations in Norway, Poland and Canada.

fortum.name: Fortum
fortum.summary: Fortum is a Finnish electricity and heat utility whose direct fossil CO2 emissions mainly come from gas- and coal/RDF/biomass-fired CHP and condensing power plants in Finland and Poland, while its largest generation portfolio is hydro and nuclear in Finland and Sweden.
subsidiaries: Fortum Power and Heat Polska Sp. z o.o.

china-huadian.summary: China Huadian is a Chinese state-owned power generation group whose emissions are dominated by coal- and gas-fired power plants and coal-related operations in China, with significant overseas thermal power assets in Indonesia and Cambodia and smaller fossil-fuel power exposure in Russia.
subsidiaries: 中国华电集团有限公司

rosneft.name: Rosneft
rosneft.summary: Rosneft is Russia’s state-controlled integrated oil and gas group, with its largest emissions from Russian oil and gas production, gas processing, petrochemicals and refineries, plus refinery interests in Germany and India.

lukoil.name: Lukoil
lukoil.summary: Lukoil is a Russian vertically integrated oil and gas group whose major emitting assets include upstream oil and gas production, gas processing, power/heat generation and large refineries in Russia—Perm, Volgograd, Nizhny Novgorod/Kstovo and Ukhta—plus refineries in Bulgaria and Romania and a 45% stake in the Netherlands’ Zeeland refinery; its large non-Russian upstream footprint includes Iraq, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Egypt. Sources: Lukoil states that its refining system comprises four Russian refineries, two European refineries and a 45% interest in Zeeland, and that upstream operations span 14 countries concentrated in Russia, Central Asia and the Middle East; Lukoil group-structure disclosures identify the Russian refinery operators as LLC LUKOIL-Permnefteorgsintez, LLC LUKOIL-Volgogradneftepererabotka, LLC LUKOIL-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez and LLC LUKOIL-Ukhtaneftepererabotka; recent market reporting and sanctions coverage identify Petrotel-LUKOIL in Romania and LUKOIL Neftohim Burgas in Bulgaria as key subsidiaries/refining assets.

surgutneftegas.name: Surgutneftegas
surgutneftegas.summary: Surgutneftegas is a Russian vertically integrated oil and gas group whose major emissions arise from oil and gas production in Western Siberia, Eastern Siberia and Timan-Pechora, associated-gas processing and power generation, and the KINEF oil refinery at Kirishi in Leningrad Oblast, Russia.

novatek.name: NOVATEK
novatek.summary: NOVATEK is a Russian independent natural-gas producer whose major emissions are from gas and condensate production in the Yamal-Nenets/Gydan areas and from LNG, gas-condensate processing and fractionation assets such as Yamal LNG, Arctic LNG 2, Purovsky, Ust-Luga and Cryogas-Vysotsk in Russia.

severstal.name: Severstal
severstal.summary: Severstal is a vertically integrated Russian steel and mining group whose largest emissions are from the Cherepovets integrated steelworks and associated captive power, plus Russian iron-ore, coking-coal, pipe, metalware and scrap operations.

nlmk.name: NLMK
nlmk.summary: NLMK is a Russia-headquartered vertically integrated steel group whose largest emissions are from its Lipetsk blast-furnace/basic-oxygen steelworks, Russian coke, iron ore and flux mining operations, and additional steelmaking/rolling assets in Russia, the United States and Europe.
subsidiaries: Public Joint Stock Company Novolipetsk Steel
Stoilensky Mining and Beneficiation Plant JSC

mmk.name: MMK
mmk.summary: MMK is a Russian integrated steel group centered on the Magnitogorsk iron and steel complex in Chelyabinsk Oblast, with additional steelmaking/rolling operations in Turkey through MMK Metalurji and coal-mining assets in Russia’s Kemerovo region through Belon/MMK-Ugol.
subsidiaries: Public Joint Stock Company Magnitogorsk Iron & Steel Works
Magnitogorsk Iron and Steel Works PJSC

evraz.name: EVRAZ
evraz.summary: EVRAZ is a UK-incorporated, Russia-centered vertically integrated steel, iron ore, coal and vanadium group whose largest emitting assets are integrated steelworks, coke/power units, iron-ore and coal mines in Russia, with smaller steel/vanadium operations in Kazakhstan and Czechia and formerly major North American steel mills in the USA and Canada before the July 2025 sale of EVRAZ North America.
subsidiaries: EVRAZ Kachkanarsky Mining-and-Processing Integrated Works / EVRAZ KGOK
